1	You are adjudicating disagreements between a benchmark case's answer key and an independent expert's blind solution. For each flagged item, rule whether the key's answer is uniquely defensible from the evidence (key-uniquely-defensible), whether two answers are defensible (ambiguous), or whether the key is wrong (key-wrong). If not uniquely defensible, propose the smallest change to the case evidence or the key that would make exactly one answer defensible.

3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.
8	- Items with asOfStage set must be answered using only evidence whose stage is at or before that stage.

333	CASE OD2-HO-SEQ-1 (SEQ, technical): Soft pedals at Eastgate depot
334	Setting: Larkspur Parcel Co. runs 140 light delivery vans from three depots: Eastgate (38 vans, LK-201 to LK-238), Millbrook (44) and Harrow Lane (58). Eastgate's vans are maintained in an in-house brake bay, which was closed for refurbishment from 4 August to 19 September. In 2025 the company changed several things in quick succession: a new front-pad supplier (Tessaro Friction) from 1 July, a defect-reporting app (FleetCheck) at all depots from 1 August, and a new set of hilly delivery routes (Upper Wend) run from Eastgate starting 1 September. Since early September, Eastgate drivers have been reporting brake problems, and one van nearly crashed.
335	Presenting request: The Regional Operations Director wants a decision by Friday. What is causing the cluster of soft-pedal and fade complaints at Eastgate, and what should the company do this week? She is minded to discipline drivers who keep complaining and retrain everyone on descent braking.
336	INITIAL EVIDENCE
337	E1 [stage S1] Email from Mariana Selby, Regional Operations Director, to fleet analyst, 13 Oct (leadership-account): Subject: Eastgate brakes – need a call by Friday. Since early September Eastgate drivers have logged 27 soft-pedal or fade complaints. On 9 October LK-209 lost most of its braking on the Carrow Hill descent. The driver stopped it with gears and the handbrake, and nobody was hurt. LK-209 is parked. My view: this started the week we launched Upper Wend, and Upper Wend is the only hilly work we have. I think drivers are riding the brakes all the way down. I'm minded to issue written warnings to the repeat complainers (some have filed three or four) and put everyone through descent retraining. Tell me if I'm wrong, with evidence.
338	E2 [stage S1] FleetCheck defect-report extract, brake categories, 1 Jul–31 Oct (system-record): Soft pedal / fade category. Eastgate (38 vans): 0 reports Jul–Aug; 27 reports Sep–Oct on 11 vans (count; first–last report): LK-203 (3; 4 Sep–21 Oct), LK-205 (2; 11 Sep–9 Oct), LK-207 (3; 2 Sep–27 Oct), LK-209 (4; 8 Sep–9 Oct), LK-211 (2; 15 Sep–16 Oct), LK-217 (3; 3–22 Sep), LK-220 (2; 18 Sep–24 Oct), LK-222 (2; 9 Sep–13 Oct), LK-224 (2; 5–23 Sep), LK-230 (2; 22 Sep–30 Oct), LK-233 (2; 26 Sep–28 Oct). Millbrook (44 vans) and Harrow Lane (58 vans) together: 2 reports Sep–Oct. Typical free text: 'fine at the top, pedal long by the bottom of Carrow Hill'. Note: FleetCheck replaced paper defect sheets at all three depots on 1 Aug.
339	E3 [stage S1] Interview notes, Tom Rudd, Eastgate depot manager, 14 Oct (manager-account): Rudd: 'Upper Wend went live on 1 September. Long downhill runs, Carrow Hill is the worst, and it takes eight or nine vans a day. Before that we were all flat suburbs. The timing speaks for itself.' On maintenance: the in-house brake bay was closed for refurbishment 4 Aug–19 Sep. Workshop coordinator Dev Okafor booked brake services that fell due in that period with Northfield Motor Services or Calder Road Garage, whichever had a slot first. 'Both fitted the Tessaro pads we supplied and did the standard two-year fluid change off the same job sheet, so that's not it.' The fleet engineer checked three complaint vans on 26 Sep and found no fault. Okafor is on leave until November.
340	E4 [stage S1] Meeting note, Priya Nandakumar, driver and union representative, 15 Oct (staff-account): 'This isn't about how we drive. Plenty of us have done Upper Wend, and we all take turns on it. What changed is the pads. Head office switched to Tessaro in July because they were cheaper, and since then you hear squealing everywhere. Cheap pads on steep hills, they cook. And now people are scared to report in case they get a warning.' She asked that drivers who reported faults not be disciplined. Asked which vans have which pads or where vans were serviced, she said she did not know.
341	E5 [stage S1] Procurement change record PCR-0417 with fleet engineering note (change-record): PCR-0417, effective 1 Jul: front brake pads for all depots switched from the previous supplier to Tessaro Friction. Pads are fitted as vans fall due for them, not as a campaign. By 30 Sep, 81 of 140 vans (58%) had Tessaro pads. Fleet engineering note, 6 Oct: 'Noise/squeal reports fleet-wide: 5 in Apr–Jun, 21 in Jul–Sep, 17 of the 21 on Tessaro-fitted vans. Caution: Tessaro vans are by definition the ones with freshly fitted pads, and we have no noise data on fresh pads of the old brand. FleetCheck also replaced paper defect sheets from 1 Aug.'
342	CATALOGUE (full contents)
343	C1 [stage S1] Telematics braking-event summary by depot, August–October - Fleet telematics platform report (telemetry): Harsh-braking events per 100 km. Eastgate: Aug 2.4, Sep 3.3, Oct 3.2. Millbrook: 2.5, 2.6, 2.7. Harrow Lane: 2.3, 2.2, 2.6. Eastgate Upper Wend route segments only, Sep–Oct: 4.6. Average speed at the top of the Carrow Hill descent: 31 mph (limit 30). Per-van and per-driver breakdowns are not enabled on the current licence, so events cannot be attributed to individual vans or drivers.
344	C2 [stage S1] Tessaro Friction batch test certificates and supplier letter - Tessaro Friction account manager, letter dated 20 Oct (vendor-account): Certificates attached for batches T-0612 and T-0703. Letter: 'Both batches tested within our published friction band at 100–350°C, and the fade test was passed. We supply more than 40 fleet customers and have no other fade reports for these batches. Pad material does not affect pedal travel unless pads are worn or wrongly fitted. We are happy to support any joint investigation.' The certificates are the supplier's own tests. No independent test is on file.
345	C3 [stage S1] Calder Road Garage job cards, stores records and correspondence for Larkspur vans, August–September - Calder Road Garage, supplied on request (document): Job cards 6 Aug–18 Sep, 12 vans: LK-201/204/206/210/212/215/218/221/225/228/231/236. Each card: front pads fitted (customer-supplied Tessaro), brake fluid changed 'from sealed 1 L bottles', pressure bleed, road test passed. Stores record: brake fluid bought in 1 L bottles and rotated by date. LK-218 card notes 'nearside slide pin seized, freed and greased'. Invoices match the cards. Correspondence: invoices and booking emails only. No warranty returns.
346	C4 [stage S1] Fleet engineer's inspection notes on three complaint vans, 26 September - A. Brandt, Larkspur fleet engineer (expert-account): Vans inspected: LK-203, LK-211, LK-230. Pad thickness 10–11 mm, discs within limits, no fluid leaks, reservoir level correct, fluid clear. Pedal firm in a static test. A 10 km road test on flat roads found no fault. Conclusion: 'No mechanical fault found. Pattern fits heat build-up from riding the brakes on long descents; suggest a descent-technique briefing.' Brandt notes that Eastgate has no brake-fluid boiling-point tester and none was used.
347	C5 [stage S1] Upper Wend route survey: gradients and descent lengths - Route planning team survey, August (document): Carrow Hill: 1.8 km at an average 9%, with a sharp left at the foot. Mill Brow: 1.1 km at 7%. Wend Lane: 0.9 km at 8%. A typical Upper Wend route has 4–6 significant descents and 70–90 drops per shift. Planner's note: 'Steepest work in the network; recommend lower gear on Carrow Hill.' No brake-temperature measurements were taken during the survey.
348	C6 [stage S1] Fleet maintenance system export: Eastgate service history and daily van assignments, June–October - Larkspur fleet maintenance system (system-record): Brake services (front pads + fluid change) by workshop. Northfield Motor Services, 4 Aug–12 Sep: 13 vans, LK-203/205/207/209/211/214/217/220/222/224/227/230/233; pads Tessaro T-0612 ×7, T-0703 ×6. Calder Road Garage, 6 Aug–18 Sep: 12 vans; T-0612 ×5, T-0703 ×7. In-house bay, Jun–Jul and 22 Sep–28 Oct: 13 vans; Tessaro ×11, previous brand ×2. Remarks: LK-217 and LK-224 'warranty return to Northfield 24 Sep, see garage paperwork'; both back in the pool 25 Sep, with 7 and 6 Upper Wend days since then. Sep–Oct assignments: vans are issued from a common pool, and each of the 38 vans ran Upper Wend on 9–16 days. The 27 soft-pedal reports came from 19 drivers. Those drivers also logged 604 days in non-Northfield vans, 141 of them on Upper Wend, with no brake reports.
349	C7 [stage S1] Eastgate driver interviews, six drivers, 14 October - Notes by Eastgate depot supervisor (staff-account): Four of the six said some vans 'go long on Carrow Hill' and others don't, and two named LK-207 and LK-209.
